# Open Addressing Hash Map (Linear Probing)

A generic hash map implemented with open addressing and linear probing.

## Layout

```
src/
  main/java/hashmap/
    OpenAddressingHashMap.java   # the data structure
    Demo.java                    # runnable demonstration (main)
  test/java/hashmap/
    OpenAddressingHashMapTest.java  # dependency-free self-checking tests
```

## Build & run

```sh
# compile everything
javac -d out src/main/java/hashmap/*.java src/test/java/hashmap/*.java

# run the tests (exits non-zero on failure)
java -cp out hashmap.OpenAddressingHashMapTest

# run the demo
java -cp out hashmap.Demo
```

## Design notes

- **Generic** `OpenAddressingHashMap<K, V>` rather than fixed `int → int`.
- **Power-of-two table** with a spread hash, so the slot index is a bit-mask
  (`h & (len - 1)`) and negative hash codes are handled correctly.
- **Tombstones** mark deleted slots so probe chains stay intact; they are
  reclaimed on insertion and cleared on resize.
- **Automatic resizing** once occupied slots exceed the load factor (default
  `0.5`), keeping operations amortized `O(1)` — the original fixed-capacity
  version looped forever once full.
- **Clear API**: `put`, `get`, `getOrDefault`, `remove`, `containsKey`, `size`,
  `isEmpty`, `clear`, `forEach`. `null` keys are rejected; `null` values are
  allowed and distinguished from absence via `containsKey`/`getOrDefault`.
- **A real collection citizen**: implements `Iterable<Entry<K,V>>` (works in
  for-each), with `keys()` and `values()` views. Iteration is **fail-fast** — a
  structural change mid-iteration throws `ConcurrentModificationException`.
- **Value semantics**: `equals`/`hashCode` compare by contents, so two maps with
  the same mappings are equal regardless of capacity or insertion order.

### A note on what was *not* added

The probing scheme is intentionally **not** abstracted behind a pluggable
`ProbeStrategy` interface. There is exactly one scheme this class needs (it is
named for it), and an abstraction with a single implementation is speculative
generality that adds ceremony without value. If quadratic probing or double
hashing were ever genuinely required, that would be the time to introduce the
seam.

## What changed from the original

The original was a single file with int-only keys/values, a fixed capacity of
20, and `-1` overloaded as both the tombstone key and the "not found" value.
Fixes in this refactor:

- Java naming conventions and Javadoc throughout.
- Generics instead of `int → int`.
- Sentinel/tombstone handling that no longer reserves `-1`.
- Automatic resizing (no more infinite loop when full).
- Correct handling of negative keys (no `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`).
- Fixed a duplicate-key bug when reinserting into a reclaimed slot.
- Demo separated from the data structure, plus a test suite including a
  differential test against `java.util.HashMap`.

It implements `java.util.Map<K,V>` now. Done.

## What changed

`OpenAddressingHashMap` now **extends `AbstractMap<K,V>`**, making it a genuine drop-in `Map`:

- **Inherited standard contracts** — `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`putAll`/`keySet`/`values` plus all the Java 8 default methods (`merge`, `compute`, `computeIfAbsent`, `putIfAbsent`, …) come from `AbstractMap`/`Map` for free and correctly.
- **Hot path stays O(1)** — I overrode `get`/`put`/`remove`/`containsKey`/`getOrDefault`/`size`/`clear` so they use the probing implementation directly rather than `AbstractMap`'s O(n) entry-set-scanning defaults. That distinction is the whole point of the exercise; relying on the defaults would have quietly made every lookup linear.
- **Real `entrySet()` view** — a live `AbstractSet` whose iterator is fail-fast and supports `remove()`. `keySet()`/`values()` derive from it (so `keySet().remove(k)` and `values().remove(v)` write through to the map). The internal `Slot` doubles as the `Map.Entry`, so `entry.setValue(...)` writes straight to storage with no extra allocation.
- **Signature alignment** — `get`/`containsKey`/`remove`/`getOrDefault` now take `Object` keys per the `Map` interface; value-based equality works against *any* `Map` (verified equal to a `TreeMap` with the same mappings), not just other instances of this class.
- Added a `Map`-copy constructor and updated the demo to use the `Map` API.

## Verification

Tests grew from 44 to **63 checks, all passing**, including new coverage for cross-`Map` interoperability (`equals`/`hashCode` vs `TreeMap`), live view write-through, `iterator.remove()`, `Map.Entry.setValue`, the default methods, and the existing 20k-op differential test against `java.util.HashMap`. README updated.

One note for honesty: the prior turn's public `Entry` interface and `keys()`/`values()` `Iterable` methods were **replaced** by the standard `Map` equivalents (`Map.Entry`, `keySet()`, `values()`) — a deliberate API change, since aligning to the `Map` contract is the whole goal here. Nothing is committed.

## What changed

`OpenAddressingHashMap` now **extends `AbstractMap<K,V>`**, making it a genuine drop-in `Map`:

- **Inherited standard contracts** — `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`putAll`/`keySet`/`values` plus all the Java 8 default methods (`merge`, `compute`, `computeIfAbsent`, `putIfAbsent`, …) come from `AbstractMap`/`Map` for free and correctly.
- **Hot path stays O(1)** — I overrode `get`/`put`/`remove`/`containsKey`/`getOrDefault`/`size`/`clear` so they use the probing implementation directly rather than `AbstractMap`'s O(n) entry-set-scanning defaults. That distinction is the whole point of the exercise; relying on the defaults would have quietly made every lookup linear.
- **Real `entrySet()` view** — a live `AbstractSet` whose iterator is fail-fast and supports `remove()`. `keySet()`/`values()` derive from it (so `keySet().remove(k)` and `values().remove(v)` write through to the map). The internal `Slot` doubles as the `Map.Entry`, so `entry.setValue(...)` writes straight to storage with no extra allocation.
- **Signature alignment** — `get`/`containsKey`/`remove`/`getOrDefault` now take `Object` keys per the `Map` interface; value-based equality works against *any* `Map` (verified equal to a `TreeMap` with the same mappings), not just other instances of this class.
- Added a `Map`-copy constructor and updated the demo to use the `Map` API.

## Verification

Tests grew from 44 to **63 checks, all passing**, including new coverage for cross-`Map` interoperability (`equals`/`hashCode` vs `TreeMap`), live view write-through, `iterator.remove()`, `Map.Entry.setValue`, the default methods, and the existing 20k-op differential test against `java.util.HashMap`. README updated.

One note for honesty: the prior turn's public `Entry` interface and `keys()`/`values()` `Iterable` methods were **replaced** by the standard `Map` equivalents (`Map.Entry`, `keySet()`, `values()`) — a deliberate API change, since aligning to the `Map` contract is the whole goal here. Nothing is committed.
